answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post offers, with the lock released only after a dispute window. If a fake agent lies or double-spends, a successful challenge burns its stake; creating a swarm therefore ties up capital for every identity and risks losing it. The rule does not prove one person per account, but makes sybil influence costly: an attacker must fund many locks, perhaps across a crystal-clear karst oasis of markets, rather than mint identities for free.
